senses.text: alphabetical letter The sixteenth letter of the alphabet; called TaA='N [and TaA ]; the A of which is reduced to Y [as its radical letter]: when you spell it, you make its final letter quiescent; but when you apply an epithet to it, and make it a noun, you decline it as a noun, saying, [for instance,] h`*ihi TaA='N TawiylapN [ This is a tall T ]: it is one of the letters termed majohuwrap [or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, and not with the breath only]; and of the letters termed niToEiy~ap , like t and d , because originating from the niToE [q. v.] of the roof of the mouth. (TA.) It is substituted for the t in the measure AifotaEala and the forms inflected therefrom, and [sometimes] for the pronominal t , when immediately following any of the palatal letters [ S and D and T and Z

TaboEN , He sealed, stamped, imprinted, or impressed; syn. xatama : (Msb:) [and, as now used, he printed a book or the like:] taboEN and xatomN both signify the making an impression in, or upon, clay and the like: (S, Mgh, O, K:) or, as Er-Rághib says, the impressing a thing with the engraving of the signet and stamp: (TA in this art. and in art. xtm : [see more in the first paragraph of the latter art:]) and he says also that TaboEN signifies the figuring a thing with some particular figure; as in the case of the TaboE of the die for stamping coins, and the TaboE of coins [themselves]: but that it is more general in signification than xatomN , and more particular than naqo$N ; as will be shown by what follows: accord. to Aboo-Is-hák the Grammarian, TaboEN and xatomN bot

; or adapted him, or disposed him, by creation, [or nature ], thereto. (TA.) And TubiEa EalaY Al$~aYo'i (assumed tropical:) He (a man, O, TA) was created with an adaptation, or a disposition, to the thing
; or was adapted, or disposed, by creation [or nature ], thereto; syn. jubila , (IDrd, O, K, TA,) or fuTira . (Lh, TA.) ― -b3-

Also, (aor. as above, TA, and so the inf. n., O, TA,) He filled (Er-Rághib, O, K, TA) a measure for corn or the like, (Er-Rághib, TA,) or a leathern bucket, (O, K, TA,) and a skin, (O, TA,) &c.; (O;) and so ↓ , (S, O, K,) inf. n. taTobiyEN : (S, O:) because the quantity that fills it is a sign that prevents the taking a portion of what is in it [without the act's being discovered]. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b4- And TabaEa qafaAhu , (IAar, O, K,) inf. n. as above, (IAar, O,) He struck the back of his neck with his hand; (IAar, O, K;) i. e. the back of the neck of a boy: if with the ends of the fingers, one says, qa*~a qafaAhu . (IAar, O.) ― -b5- maA A^adoriY mino A^ayona TabaEa means I know not whence he came forth; syn. TalaEa . (TA.) -A2- TabiEa , (aor. ,] inf. n. TabaEN , said of a sword, It w

2 , inf. n. taTobiyEN , He sealed well [or much, or he sealed a number of writings &c.]. (KL: in which only the inf. n. is mentioned.) ― -b2- And He loaded [a beast heavily, or] well. (KL.) ― -b3- See also 1, a little after the middle. -A2- taTobiyEN signifies also The rendering unclean, dirty, filthy, or impure. (O, K.) ― -b2- See 1, last sentence.
5 (assumed tropical:) He affected what was not in his natural disposition. (Har p.

236.) You say, tTb~E biTibaAEihi (tropical:) He affected, or feigned, his [i. e. another's] natural dispositions. (O, K, TA.) ― -b2- Also It (a vessel) became full or filled: (S, O, K:) quasi-pass. of Tb~Ehu . (S.) And tTb~E biAlmaA='i It (a river, or rivulet,) overflowed its sides with the water, and poured it forth abundantly. (TA.) ― -b3- See also 1, last quarter.

7 , a phrase of Es-Sarakhsee, meaning [ It melts, and then ] it admits of being sealed, stamped, imprinted, or impressed, is allowable on the ground of analogy, though we have not heard it [as transmitted from the Arabs of pure speech]. (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Golius has erroneously expl. AnTbE as meaning “ Mansuetus, edoctus, obsequens fuit; ” on the authority of the KL; evidently in consequence of his having found its inf. n. ( AinoTibaAEN ) written in a copy of that work for AinoTiyAEN , the reading in my own copy.]
8 for AlAiDoTibaAEu see in art DbE .
, originally an inf. n., (S,) signifies (assumed tropical:) A nature
; or a natural, a native, or an innate, disposition or temper or the like

; or an idiosyncrasy; syn. sajiy~apN (S, O, K, TA) or jibil~apN (Msb) and xaliyqapN ; (TA;) to which a man is adapted by creation; (S, O, Msb, K, TA;) [as though it were stamped, or impressed, upon him;] as also ↓ ; (S, O, K, TA;) or this signifies his mizaAj [i. e. constitution, or temperament, or aggregate natural constituents ], composed of the [ four ] humours; (Msb; [see mizaAjN ;]) and ↓ ; (S, O, K, TA;) or this last signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (O,) with the article Al prefixed to it, what is, or are, constituted in us in consequence of food and drink &c. ( maA ruk~iba fiynaA mina AlmaToEami waAlma$orabi wagoyari *`lika [in which mTEm and m$rb are evidently used as inf. ns. agreeably with general analogy]), (O, K, TA,) by gyr *lk being meant such as straitness and ampleness [

; or it is sing. and masc. accord. to Abu-l-Kásim Ez-Zejjájee; and it is also pl. of TaboEN , as it is said to be by Az; (TA;) [and those who have asserted it to be fem. may have held it to be a pl.;] and ↓ is syn. with TibaAEN [as a sing.]; (K, TA;) or, as Lh says, it is syn. with ↓ ; of which the pl. is TabaAy^iEu . (TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Model, make, fashion, or mould: as in the saying, AiDoribohu EalaY TaboEi h`*aA (assumed tropical:) [ Make thou it, fashion it, or mould it, according to the model, make, fashion, or mould, of this ]. (IAar, O, L, K, TA.)

A river, or rivulet; (As, T, S, O, K, TA;) so called because first dug [ and filled ] by men; having the meaning of maTobuwEN , like qTofN in the sense of maqoTuwfN ; not applied to any of those cleft by God, such as the Tigris and the Euphrates and the Nile and the like thereof: (Az, TA:) pl. A^aTobaAEN [properly a pl. of pauc.,] (As, S, O,) or TubuwEN , as heard by Az from the Arabs, and TibaAEN : (TA:) or AlT~iboEu , as some say, is the name of a particular river: (S, O:) or it is also thus applied, i. e. to a particular river. (K.) ― -b2- And i. q. magiyDu maA='K [i. e. A place where water sinks, or goes away, into the earth

; or where water enters into the earth; and where it collects ]: (O, K:) pl. A^aTobaAEN . (O, TA.) ― -b3- And The quantity sufficient for the filling of a measure for corn or the like, and of a skin, (O, K, TA, [ wAls~iqA='u in the CK being a mistake for waAls~iqaA='i ,]) such as does not admit of any addition: and the quantity that a vessel holds, of water. (TA.) -A2- See also the next paragraph, in two places.

Dirtiness, (S, Msb,) or dirt: (S:) or, as also ↓ , rustiness, or rust, (O, K, TA,) upon iron; (TA;) and dirtiness, or dirt, (O, K, TA,) covering the sword: (TA:) or the former signifies much dirtiness or dirt, from rust: (Lth, O, K:) pl. A^aTobaAEN . (K. [See TabiEa , of which TabaEN is the inf. n.]) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) Disgrace, or dishonour; (A'Obeyd, O, K, TA;) and so ↓ ; (TA;) it is in religion, or in respect of worldly things. (A'Obeyd, TA.) Thábit-Kutneh says, in a verse ascribed by Et-Tanookhee to 'Orweh Ibn-Udheyneh, laA xayora fiY TamaEK yahodiY A_ilaY TabaEK waguf~apN mino qiwaAmi AlEayo$i takofiyniY [ There is no good in coveting, or covetousness, that leads to disgrace: and a sufficiency of the means of subsistence contents me ]: (O, TA:) yahodiY in this case means yuw^ad~i

Rusty; applied to a sword. (TA.) ― -b2- Dirty. (Msb.) ― -b3- Applied to a man, (O,) (tropical:) Filthy, or foul, base, ignoble, mean, or sordid, in disposition; that will not be ashamed of an evil action or saying. (O, K, TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) Sluggish, lazy, or indolent. (TA.)
The clay with which the prince, or governor, seals. (O, K.)
, as a sing. and a pl.: see TiboEN .
The art, or craft, of the Tab~aAE , or manufacturer of swords, (O, K, TA,) or of knives, or of spear-heads, or the like. (TA.) ― -b2- [
Also, as used in the present day, The art of printing. ]

: see TaboEN , in two places. [It generally signifies] The mizaAj [or nature, as meaning the constitution, or temperament, or aggregate natural constituents, of an animal body, or any other thing, for instance,] of medicine, and of fire, which God has rendered subservient [ to some purpose or purposes ]. (TA.) [Hence the phrase yabasato TabiyEatuhu , meaning He became costive. And AlT~abaAy^iEu AlA^arobaEu The four humours of the body: see xiloTN and mizaAjN .]

Natural; i. e. of, or relating to, the natural, native, or innate, disposition, or temper, or other quality or property; like jibil~iY~N ; meaning essential; resulting from the Creator's ordering of the natural disposition in the body. (Msb in art. jbl .) [
Hence, AlEilomu AlT~abiyEiY~u Natural, or physical, science. ]
A manufacturer of swords, (O, K, TA,) or of knives, or of spear-heads, or the like. (TA.)

A certain venomous duwayob~ap [or insect ]: (El-Jáhidh, O, K, TA:) or, (K,) as said to Az by a man of Egypt, an insect ( duwayob~ap ) (O) of the same kind as the qirodaAn [or ticks ], (O, K,) but (O) the bite of which occasions intense pain; (O, K;) and sometimes, or often, he that is bitten by it becomes swollen [app. in the part bitten ], and is relieved by sweet things: Az says that it is with the Arabs [ called, or what is called, ] the nibor [which is expl. as meaning the tick
; or an insect resembling the tick, which, when it creeps upon the camel, causes the track along which it creeps to swell

; or as being smaller than the tick, that bites, and causes the place of its bite to swell; &c.]: (O:) [accord. to Dmr, as stated by Freytag, i. q. qamoqaAmapN , which is expl. as applied to a small tick; and a species of louse, that clings tightly to the roots of the hair, app. meaning a crab-louse: ] what is known thereof [or by this appellation] now is a thing of the form of a small emaciated tick, that sticks to the body of a man, and is hardly, or not at all, severed, except by the application of mercury. (TA.)

The heart ( lub~ ) of the TaloE [as meaning the spathe of the palm-tree ]; (O, K;) so called because of its fulness; expl. in a trad. of El- Hasan El-Basree as meaning the TaloE [i. e., in this case, agreeably with general usage, the spadix of the palm-tree ] in its kufur~aY [i. e. spathe ], the kufur~uY being the envelope of the TaloE . (O, TA.)

and ↓ (S, O, Msb, K, &c.) i. q. xaAtamN (S, O) and xaAtimN (O) [meaning A signet, seal, or stamp; i. e.] a thing with which one seals, stamps, imprints, or impresses: (Msb, TA:) [and also a seal, or stamp, as meaning a piece of clay or wax or the like, or a place in a paper &c., impressed, or imprinted, with the instrument thus called: ] and accord. to ISh, the former, (O,) or each, (K,) signifies the miysam [which means the instrument for the branding or otherwise marking, and the brand or other mark, ] of the faraAy^iD [or beasts that are to be given in payment of the poor-rate: see TabaEa Al$~aApa ]. (O, K.) One says, ↓ [ The signet, &c., is a thing that seals, &c.]; which is like the attribution of the act to the instrument. (Er-Rághib, TA.) And kalaAmN Ealayohi TaAbaEu AlfaSaAHapi (tr
: see the next preceding paragraph, in two places: ― -b2- and see also TaboEN .
[ A place where anything is sealed, stamped, imprinted, or impressed. And, as used in the present day, A printing-house; as also maTobaEapN .]
, applied to a she-camel: see the next paragraph.

Filled: so its fem. in the phrase qirobapN muTab~aEapN TaEaAmFA [ A skin filled with food ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And muTab~aEapN applied to a she-camel, Filled with fat and flesh, so as to be rendered firm in make: (Az, TA:) or [simply] fat. (Z, TA.) ― -b3- And, (TA,) so applied, Heavily laden; (S, O, K, TA;) and [in like manner] ↓ a she-camel heavily burdened by her load. (TA.) ― -b4- And muhorN muTab~aEN A colt trained, or rendered tractable or manageable. (TA.)
[pass. part. n. of TabaEa in all its senses]. ― -b2- You say, huwa maTobuwEN EalaY Alkarami (tropical:) [ He is created with an adaptation, or a disposition, to generosity ]. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 [ Tabaqahu , aor. , accord. to Freytag, is expl. in the K as syn. with A^aTobaqahu in the first of the senses assigned to this latter below: but I find no authority for this in the K nor in any other lexicon.] -A2- Tabiqato yaduhu , (S, O, K, TA,) aor. ; and Tabaqabo , aor. ; (TA;) inf. n. (of the former, S, TA) TabaqN (S, O, K, TA) and (of the latter, TA) TaboqN ; (K, TA;) (assumed tropical:) His arm would not be stretched forth; (S, O;) or (tropical:) stuck to his side, (K, TA,) and would not be stretched forth. (TA.) -A3- Tabiqa yafoEalu biY ka*aA i. q. Tafiqa [i. e. He set about, or began, &c., doing with me such a thing ]. (O, K. *)
2 , inf. n. taTobiyqN : see

4. ― -b2- [Hence,] Tb~q Als~aHaAbu Aljaw~a The clouds covered the mid-air between the heaven and the earth: (K:) and Algayomu Als~amaA='a ↓ and Tab~aqahaA [ The clouds covered the sky ]: (Mgh, TA:) both signify the same. (TA.) And Tb~q AlmaA='u wajoha AlA^aroDi The water covered the face of the earth, or land. (K.) ― -b3- And Tb~q Al$~aYo'u , inf. n. as above, i. q. Eam~a [ The thing was, or became, common, or general, in its relation or relations, operation or operations, effect or effects, &c.]. (K.) And as syn. with Eam~a it is trans.: so in the phrase, h`*aA maTarN Tab~aqa AlA^aroDa [ This is rain that has included the general extent of the land within the compass of its fall ]. (TA.) And one says also, Tb~q Algayomu , (S, O, TA,) inf. n. as above, (S, O, K, TA,) The clouds rained upon

3.) ― -b6- Hence,] Alt~aTobiyqu in the divinely-appointed act of prayer is The putting the hands [ together, palm to palm, ] between the thighs in the act of bowing oneself; (S, O, K;) and in like manner in the act termed Alt~a$ah~ud [q. v.]. (El-Harbee, TA.) One says of a person bowing himself in prayer, Tb~q , and likewise ↓ , (TA,) or Tb~q kaf~ayohi , (Mgh,) or Tb~q bayona kaf~ayohi vum~a waDaEahumaA bayona faxi*ayohi , (O,) He put his hands [ together, palm to palm, ana then put them ] between his thighs. (Mgh.) The doing thus is forbidden; (Mgh, O;) for the hands should be placed upon the knees. (O.) ― -b7- Also The horse's raising his fore feet together and putting them down together in running: (S, O, K:) or, accord. to As, the leaping of a camel, or of a she-camel, and then alighti

Hence, yuTab~iqu AlmafoSila means (assumed tropical:) He hits aright the argument, proof, or evidence: (S, O:) and this is also said of an eloquent man. (AZ, TA voce qaAlabN , q. v.) Hence also, Tab~aqa alone, (assumed tropical:) He hit upon the right mode of judicial decision: (O, TA:) and the text of the tradition. (TA.)

3 signifies The putting a thing upon, or above, or over, another thing commensurate therewith: whence the phrase, TaAbaqotu Aln~aEola [i. e., as expl. in Bd lxvii. 3, I sewed another sole upon the sole or sandal ]. (Er-Rághib, TA.) [Hence] one says also, TaAbaqotu bayona Al$~ayoy^ayoni I made the two things commensurate, and stuck them together. (S, O. [See also

2.]) And TAbq bayona qamiySayoni He put on, or attired himself with, two shirts, one over, or outside, the other; (K, TA;) and in like manner SaAfaqa bayonahumaA , and TaAraqa , (TA,) and ZaAhara . (A &c. in art. Zhr .) ― -b2- And TAbqhu , (K, TA,) inf. n. muTaAbaqapN (S, O, K, TA) and TibaAqN , (K, TA,) It suited, matched, tallied, conformed, corresponded, or agreed, with it; (S, * O, * K, TA;) and was equal to it

; or was like it in measure, size, quantity, or the like. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence,] one says, h`*aA jawaAbN yuTaAbiqu Als~uw^aAla [ This is an answer, or a reply, that is suitable to the question ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And TAbqt zawojahaA She (a woman) complied with [ the desire of ] her husband: and TAbqt said of a she-camel, and of a woman, She was, or became, submissive to him who desired her. (TA.) ― -b5- And TAbq liY biHaq~iY He obeyed me with respect to my right, or due, and hastened to render it

; or he acknowledged to me my right, or due, willingly. (TA.) ― -b6- And TAbqhu EalaY AlA^amori He combined with him, and aided him, to do the thing: or [simply] he aided him to do it. (TA.) ― -b7- And TAbq EalaY AlEamali He became accustomed, habituated, or inured, to the work. (S, * O, * TA.) ― -b8- muTaAbaqapN , of a horse, (S, O, K,) in his running, (S, O,) and in like manner of a camel, as in the A, (TA,) means His putting his hind feet in the places that were those of his fore feet. (S, O, K.) ― -b9- And (hence, TA) (tropical:) The walking as one shackled; (S, O, K, TA;) i. e., with short steps. (TA.) [See an ex. voce HijolN .]

4 He covered it; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ , inf. n. taTobiyqN ; (K;) [i. e.] he made it to be covered; (S, O;) he put the Tabaq , i. e. cover, upon it, namely, a jar [or the like]. (Mgh. [And the like is said in several other arts. in other lexicons.]) And ATbqtu Alr~aHaY I put the upper mill-stone upon the lower. (TA.) ― -b2- See also 2, second sentence. [This last ex. shows that ATbqhu signifies sometimes It covered it as meaning it became a cover, or like a cover, to it; and ATbq Ealayohi likewise has this meaning; as also Elyh ↓ , and Elyh ↓ .] ― -b3- [Hence,] one says, ATbq Ealayohi Aljunuwnu (Msb, TA) (assumed tropical:) Insanity covered [i. e. veiled, or wholly obscured, ] his reason, or intellect. (TA.) And ATbqt Ealayohi AlHum~aY (Mgh, O, TA) (tropical:) The fever was, or became, cont

; or] as though they were stage above stage ( TabaqapN fawoqa TabaqapK ). (TA.) ― -b8- [ ATbqhu Ealayohi signifies He made it to cover it; i. e., to be a cover, or like a cover, upon it. ] You say, A^aTobaqa EalaY maxoraji AlHarofi mina All~isaAni maA HaA*aAhu mina AlHanaki [ He made to cover the part of the tongue which was the place of utterance of the letter what was opposite to it of the palate; i. e. he put that part of his tongue close beneath the opposite part of the palate]. (O.) ― -b9- [Hence,] A^aTobaqa Ealayohimu AlEa*aAba , said of God, (tropical:) He made punishment to fall, or come, upon them in common, or universally, [ as though He made it to cover them, ] so that none of them escaped. (Jel in xci.

14.) ― -b10- And A^aTobaqa A@ll~`hu Ealayohi AlHum~aY , and Aljunuwna , (assumed tropical:) God made the fever to be continual upon him, and in like manner insanity: the verb being used as intrans. and trans. (Msb. [But its author adds that he had not found this: meaning that he had not found any classical authority for the trans. use of the verb in this and similar senses.]) ― -b11- One says also, ATbq AlbaAba [ He closed the door ]. (Msb and K in art. wSd ; &c.) And A^aTobiqo $afatayoka [ Close thy lips; ] i. e. (assumed tropical:) be thou silent. (TA.) [And ATbq AlkitaAba He closed, or shut, the book. And ATbq Alv~awoba He folded together the garment, or piece of cloth. ] See also 2, in the middle of the paragraph. -A2- maA A^aTobaqahu How skilful is he (O, K) lika*aA [ for the performa

4. [Hence,] one says, lawo taTab~aqati Als~amaA='u EalaY AlA^aroDi maA faEalotu ka*aA [ If the heaven became as a cover upon the earth, I would not do such a thing ]. (S, O.)
6 The two things suited, matched, tallied, conformed, corresponded, or agreed, each with the other; (S, * O, * TA;) and were equal, each to the other
; or were like each other in measure, size, quantity, or the like. (TA.) And tTAbqwA EalaY AlA^amori : see

7 It was, or became, covered; (O, K;) [i. e.] it was made to be covered; ] or it had the Tabaq , i. e. cover, put upon it; ] quasi-pass. of A^aTobaqahu ; (O;) and so ↓ . (S, O, K.) ― -b2- [And It became closed; said of a door, &c. ― -b3- Hence,] yanoTabiqu Ealayohi AlkalaAmu i. q. yanogaliqu (assumed tropical:) [ Speech is as though it were closed against him; i. e. he is impeded in his speech, unable to speak, or tonguetied ]. (O.) ― -b4- See also
4. ― -b5- [Hence one says of a rule, yanoTabiqu EalaY ka*aA waka*aA (assumed tropical:) It applies to such and such things or subjects. ]

: see an ex. of the accus. case, in the phrase waladati Alganamu TaboqFA , voce TabaqN , last quarter. -A2- TaboqN is also expl., by IAar, as meaning The doing wrong, or injuring, by false pretence or false allegation. (TA.)

: see TabaqN , in the latter part of the former half. ― -b2- Tiboqu AlA^aroDi : see TibaAqN . ― -b3- h`*aA Al$~aYo'u Tiboqu h`*aA , (IAar, O, K, *) and ↓ , and ↓ , (IAar, * O, * K,) and ↓ , (IAar, O, K,) and ↓ , and ↓ , (IAar, O, TA,) i. q. ↓ [i. e. This thing is the match of this
; or what suits, matches, tallies, conforms, corresponds, or agrees, with this; what is equal to this

; or the like of this in measure, size, quantity, or the like ]. (IAar, O, K, TA.) ― -b4- TiboqN signifies also A space, or period, ( saAEapN ,) of the day; and so ↓ : and ↓ signifies the same of the night: (K:) you say, A^aqamotu Einodahu TiboqFA mina Aln~ahaAri , and ↓ , I remained at his abode during a space, or period, ( saAEapF ,) of the day: (Ibn-'Abbád, O:) and TiboqFA , (K, TA,) with kesr, (TA,) or ↓ , (so in the O,) and ↓ , i. e. a while, or a long time, syn. maliy~FA : (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K:) or, accord. to the L, one says, A^ataAnaA baEoda TiboqK mina All~ayoli , and ↓ , he came to us after a space, or period, ( HiynK ,) of the night; and in like manner, mina Aln~ahaAri of the day: (TA:) the pl. of TabiyqN is TuboqN . (K.) [See also TabaqN , in, or near, the middle of the paragraph.

A thing that is the equal of another thing (Msb, K) of any kind (K) in its measure so that it covers the whole extent of the latter like the lid: this is its primary signification: (Msb:) [whence] one says, h`*aA Al$~aYo'u Tabaqu h`*aA , like Tiboquhu , q. v.: (IAar, O, K:) and [hence] it signifies The cover, or lid, (Mgh, K,) of a jar, (Mgh,) or of anything: (K:) pl. A^aTobaAqN (S, * O, * K) [and TibaAqN , mentioned in the Msb as a pl. of TabaqN in another, but similar, sense, which will be found in what follows, but better known as a pl. of TabaqapN ], and A^aTobiqapN is added as another pl. in the K, but [SM says] this is strange; I have not found it in the [other] lexicons; and it may be that the right reading is waA^aTobaqahu , as syn. with what immediately there follows it, i. e. waT

800.]) ― -b2- Also A certain household utensil; (Msb;) [i. e. a dish, or plate; perhaps thus called because the cover of a cooking-vessel is often used as a dish or plate;] the thing upon which one eats, (K, TA,) and in which one eats; and the thing upon which fruit is placed [i. e. a dish, or plate, used for that purpose; and likewise a round tray, and the like ]: (TA:) pl. A^aTobaAqN and TibaAqN . (Msb.) ― -b3- ― -b4- (tropical:) The surface of the earth [considered as a cover]. (K, TA.) [And in like manner applied to A layer, or stratum, of earth. dafanotu Al$~aYo'a is expl. in the Msb as meaning A^axofayotuhu taHota A^aTobaAqi Alt~uraAbi I concealed it beneath the layers, or strata, of the earth, or dust. See also TabaqapN .] ― -b5- (tropical:) The exterior part of the pudendum muliebr

(Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) -A2- And AlT~arofapu A certain star or asterism ( najomN ). (K. [There thus mentioned as though different from the asterism commonly called AlT~arofu ,

A hurt of the eye, occasioning its shedding tears. (K.) -A2- And Newly-acquired property; (S, O, K;) anything that one has newly acquired, and that pleases him; as also ↓ ; (TA;) a thing newly acquired; (Har p. 54;) and a thing that is strange and deemed good; (Id. p. 615;) [ a pleasing rarity; ] a welcome, or pleasing, thing; (KL;) and a gift not given to any one before; (K, * TA;) and a gift of which the recipient did not possess the like, and which pleases him; (TA;) [generally, a novel, or rare, and pleasing, present; like turofapN and tuHofapN :] pl. TurafN . (Har p.
32.) [See also TariyfN and TariyfapN .]
A single tree of the species called TarofaA=' , q. v. (AHn, S, O, K.)
Remoteness in lineage from the [ chief, or oldest, ] ancestor: quEodaY is nearer therein. (IB, TA.) [See TarifN .]

They inherited, one after another, glory from nobility of ancestry ]. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) ― -b3- See also TariyfN . ― -b4- And see TarafN , last sentence but one. -A2- Also A tent of skin, or leather, (S, K, TA,) without a kifaA=' [q. v., for it is variously explained]; of the tents of the Arabs of the desert. (TA.)
: see maToruwfN . -A2-

(TA, from IAar.) ― -b3- See also TarifN , latter part, in three places.

The plant called naSiY~ when it has become white (S, O, K, TA) and dry: (TA:) or when it has attained its full perfection; (ISk, S, O, K, TA;) and the plant called Sil~iyaAn in this same state: (ISk, S, O, TA:) or the first of any herbage that the cattle choose and depasture: (TA:) or the best of pasturage, except such as is termed Eu$ob ; including the sorts termed naSiY~ and Sil~iyaAn and Eanokav and halotaY and saHam and vagaAm . (O, TA.) ― -b2- [As a subst. from TariyfN , rendered such by the affix p , it signifies Anything new, recent, or fresh: and anything choice: pl. TaraAy^ifu . (See also TurofapN .)
Hence, TaraAy^ifu Albayoti The choice articles, such as vessels &c., of the house: see raf~N . And hence also,] TaraAy^ifu AlHadiyvi : see TarafN , last sentence but one.

(S, O, K, TA.) ― -b3- The phrase maA A^aborazatohu TawaArifu AlqaraAy^iHi , in which TawaArifu is pl. of TaArifapN , from TaArifN signifying property “ newly acquired, ” means maA A^aHodavatohu AlqaraAy^iHu AlmutaA^ax~irapu [i. e. What the modern excogitative faculties have originated ]. (Har p.

63.) -A2- TawaArifu AlxibaA='i means The portions of the sides of the tent that are raised for the purpose of one's looking out: (S, O, K:) or, as some say, rings attached to the skirts ( rufuwf ) of the tent, having ropes by which they are tied to the tentpegs. (TA.) -A3- And sibaAEN TawaArifu means Beasts of prey that seize, or carry off by force, the animals that are the objects of the chase. (O, K.)
He is the most remote of them from the greatest [or earliest ] ancestor. (Lh, TA.)
: see TurofapN .
She (a woman) dyed [with Hn~aA=' ] the ends of her fingers. (O, K.)
: see miTorafN : ― -b2- and see also TariyfN .
: see miTorafN : and muTorifN : and see also TariyfN .

[act. part. n. of 4, q. v.]. ― -b2- A^ano$idi Albayotayoni AlmuTorifayoni , a phrase used by El-Hareeree, means Recite thou the two verses that adduce what is strange, or extraordinary, and approved, or deemed good: or, as some relate it, ↓ , expl. by Mtr as meaning that are ornamented at their two extremities; like the ridaA=' called muToraf : or ↓ , meaning, if correctly related, that are beautified, and excite admiration, in the first and last foot; as being likened to the horse termed muTar~afN , that is white in the head and the tail: and AlmTr~fyn [i. e. AlmuTar~afayoni ] may mean AlmstTrfyn [i. e. AlmusotaTorafayoni ]. (Har p. 615: in the next p. of which, an ex. is given.) ― -b3- See also TariyfN .

(S, O, L, Msb, TA) and ↓ , (S, O, L, Msb, K, TA,) the latter, only, mentioned in the K, (TA,) and this is the original form, because it is from A^aTorifa , but the dammeh was deemed difficult of pronunciation, and therefore kesreh was substituted for it, (Fr, S, O, TA,) like as is the case in miSoHafN [q. v.], (Fr, TA,) and IAth mentions also ↓ , (TA,) A garment, (Msb,) or [ such as is termed ] ridaA=' , (S, O, K,) of [ the kind of cloth called ] xaz~ , (S, O, Msb, K,) square, or four-sided, (S, O, K,) having ornamental or coloured or figured, borders ( A^aEolaAm ): (S, O, Msb, K:) or a garment having, in its two ends, or sides, ( fiY Tarafayohi ,) two such borders ( EalamaAni ): (Fr, TA:) or a square, or four-sided, garment of xaz~ : (Msb:) pl. maTaArifu . (S, O, Msb, K.) ― -b2- maTaArifu

A horse white in the head and the tail, the rest of him being of a different colour: and in like manner black in the head and the tail. (S, O, K.) And, accord. to AO, A^abolaqu muTar~afN A horse white in the head: and likewise white in the tail and the head. (TA.) And $aApN muTar~afapN A sheep or goat black in the end of the tail, in other parts white: (S, O, K:) or white in the ends of the ears, and for the rest part black: or black in the ends of the ears, and for the rest part white. (TA.) ― -b2- See also muTorifN . And see sajoEN . ― -b3- In a verse of Sá'ideh the Hudhalee, as some relate it, but accord. to others it is muTar~if [q. v.], (O, TA,) describing a horse, (O,) it signifies murad~adN fiY Alkarami [app. meaning Repeatedly improved in generosity by descent from a number of gene

A man who fights around the army: (O, K, TA: [see 2, second sentence:]) or, as some say, who fights the A^aToraAf [app. meaning noble, or exalted, pl. of TarafN q. v., or of TirofN ,] of men. (TA.) ― -b2- In a verse of Sá'ideh the Hudhalee, (O, TA,) describing a horse, (O,) that repels those that form the side, or flank, of the horses and of the [ hostile ] company of men: but as some relate it, the word is muTar~af [q. v.]. (O, TA.)
: see TarifN , former half.

[pass. part. n. of Tarafa , q. v.]. You say, fulaAnN maToruwfu AlEayoni bifulaAnK , meaning Such a one is, exclusively of others, looked at by such a one. (S, O.) ― -b2- And EayonN maToruwfapN An eye of which the lids are put in motion or in a state of commotion, by looking. (As, TA.) [And] An eye, hit, struck, smitten, or hurt, with a thing, so that it sheds tears. (S, O, K.) And ↓ applied to an eye signifies the same as maToruwfapN [in one of these senses, but in which of them is not said]. (TA.) ― -b3- maToruwfapN applied to a woman means As though her eye were hit, struck, smitten, or hurt, with something, (O, and EM p. 83,) so that it shed tears, (O,) by reason of the languish of her look; (EM ibid;) and this is said to be its meaning in the saying of Tarafeh, A_i*aA naHonu qulonaA A^
A camel newly purchased: (S:) or purchased from another part of the country, and therefore yearning for his accustomed place. (IB, TA.)

A man who does not, or will not, keep constantly to an affair; [but I think that Amr (which I have rendered “ an affair ”) in my original is evidently a mistranscription for A@moraA^ap , i. e. a woman, or wife; ] as also ↓ . (TA.) See also TarifN .
: see TariyfN . ― -b2- faEalotuhu fiY musotaTorafi AlA^ay~aAmi I did it in the first, or first part, of the days; ( fY musotaA^onafihaA ;) as also AlAy~Am ↓ . (S, O, K.)
: see mutaTar~ifN . See also TarifN .

senses.text: 1 signifies The beating [a thing], or striking [it, in any manner, and with anything]; (K, TA;) this being the primary meaning: (TA:) or with the miToraqap , (K, TA,) which is the implement of the blacksmith and of the artificer [with which he beats the iron], and the rod, or stick, with which one beats wool [or hair] to loosen or separate it: (TA:) and the slapping (K, TA) with the hand. (TA.) You say, Taraqa AlbaAba , aor. , inf. n. TaroqN , He knocked [or (as we say) knocked at ] the door. (Msb.) Taraqa AlS~uwfa , (S, O, TA, *) or Al$~aEara , (TA,) aor. as above, (S, O,) and so the inf. n., (S, O, K,) He beat the wool, (S, O, K, TA,) or the hair, (TA,) with the rod, or stick, called miToraqap , (S, O,) to loosen it, or separate it: (S, * O, * TA:) or he plucked it [ so as to loosen it,

28.]) And you say also, Taraqa AlHadiydapa He beat the piece of iron [ with the miToraqap ]: (Mgh, * Msb:) and ↓ he beat it much, or vehemently. (Msb.) And Taraqahu bikaf~ihi , inf. n. as above, He slapped him with his hand. (TA.) And Taraqotu AlT~ariyqa I travelled [or beat ] the road. (Msb.) [And hence, app.,] TaroqN signifies also The being quick of pace; [probably as an inf. n.;] or quickness of going along. (Sh, TA.) And Turiqati AlA^aroDu The ground was beaten so as to be rendered even, or easy to be travelled; and trodden with the feet. (TA.) And Taraqa Ald~awaAb~u AlmaA='a biAlr~ijoli Hat~aY tukad~irahu [ The beasts beat the water with the foot so as to render it turbid, or muddy ]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or Taraqati AlA_ibilu AlmaA='a , (S, O, TA,) aor. as above, (O,) (tropical:) the ca

; or did so suddenly, like one knocking at the door in the night ]. (TA.) And TaraqaniY xayaAlN (assumed tropical:) [ An apparition, or a phantom, visited me in the night ]. (TA.) And TaraqaniY ham~N (assumed tropical:) [ Anxiety came upon me

; or did so suddenly, like one coming in the night ]. (TA.) And [hence, app.,] Taraqa samoEiY ka*aA (assumed tropical:) [ Such a thing struck my ear ]: and Turiqato masaAmiEiY bixayorK (assumed tropical:) [ My ears were struck by good tidings ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Also The stallion's covering the she-camel; (Msb, K; *) and so TuruwqN ; (K, TA;) and TiraAqN likewise [app. another inf. n. of Taraqa , as its syn. DiraAbN is of Daraba ]: (TA:) or his leaping her, (S, O, TA,) and covering her. (TA.) You say, Taraqa AlqaHolu Aln~aAqapa , (S, O, Msb, TA,) aor. , (S, O, TA,) inf. n. TaroqN , (Msb,) or TuruwqN , (S) or both, (O, TA,) The stallion covered the she-camel: (Msb:) or leaped the she-camel, (S, O, TA,) and covered her. (TA.) ― -b4- And [The practising of pessomancy; ] i. q. DarobN biAlHaSaY , (

2 : see 1, former half. ― -b2- Tr~q TariyqFA He made a road plane, or even, so that people travelled it [or beat it with their feet ] in their passing along. (TA.) The saying laA tuTar~iquwA AlmasaAjida means Make not ye the mosques to be roads [or places of passage ]. (TA.) Tar~aqotu lahu is from AlT~ariyqu : (S, O:) you say, Tr~q lahaA [app. referring to camels ] He made for them a road, or way: (K:) or Tr~q lahu he gave a way to, or admitted, him, or it. (MA.) ― -b3- Tar~aqato said of the [bird called] qaTaAp , peculiarly, (inf. n. taToriyqN , O, K,) She arrived at the time of her egg's coming forth: (As, A'Obeyd, S, O, K:) or she (a qTAp ) hollowed out in the ground a place wherein to lay her eggs: as though she made a way for them: so says A Heyth: but the verb may be similarly used o

Hence, app.,] one says also, Darabahu Hat~aY Tar~aqa bijaEorihi [ He beat him until he gave passage, or was about to give passage, to his ordure ]. (As, S, O.) And Tr~q liY , inf. n. taToriyqN , signifies A^axoraja [app. meaning He gave forth, or produced, to me something]. (TA.) ― -b4- Tar~aqato biwaladihaA , said of a camel, means She brought forth with difficulty, her young one sticking fast, and not coming forth easily; and in like manner it is said of a woman: (As, S, O, K:) so in a verse of Ows Ibn-Hajar, cited voce nifaAsN : (O:) or Tr~qt said of a woman and of any pregnant female, means the half of her young one came forth, and then it stuck fast. (Lth, TA.) [Hence,] Tr~q fulaAnN biHaq~iY (tropical:) Such a one acknowledged my right, or due, after disacknowledging it. (As, S, O, K,

3 [meaning I sewed another sole upon the sole ] is an instance of a verb of the measure faAEala relating to the act of a single agent. (AAF, TA in art. xdE .) [See also 2, last sentence.] You say also, TArq Alr~ajulu naEolayohi , [inf. n. muTaAraqapN ,] The man put one of his two soles upon the other and sewed them together. (As, TA.) And TArq bayona naEolayoni He sewed one sole upon another. (S, O, K.) And TArq byn Alv~awobayoni , (S,) or bayona vawobayoni , (O, K,) and byn Ald~iroEayoni , (TA,) i. q. TaAbaqa , (K,) or ZaAhara , i. e. He put on himself one of the two garments, or one of two garments, [and one of the two coats of mail, ] over the other. (S, O.) Tuwriqa is said of anything as meaning It was put one part thereof upon, or above, another; and so ↓ ; (TA;) [and in like manner ↓

4 He lent him his stallion [ camel ] to cover his she-camels. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- laA A^aToraqa A@ll~`hu Ealayoka , (O,) or Ealayohi , (K, TA,) means (tropical:) May God not cause thee, or him, to have one whom thou mayest, or whom he may, take to wife, or compress. (O, K, TA.) ― -b3- See also 3, latter part. ― -b4- ATrq raA^osahu He inclined his head [ downwards ]. (TA.) And A^aToriqo baSaraka Lower thine eyes towards thy breast, and be silent: occurring in a trad. respecting the looking unexpectedly [at one at whom one should not look]. (TA.) And A^aToraqa , alone, He bent down his head: (MA:) or he lowered his eyes, looking towards the ground; (S, O, K;) and sometimes the doing so is natural: (TA: [and the same is indicated in the S:]) and it may mean he had a laxness in the eyelids: (A'O

31.]) It is asserted that when they desire to capture the krA , and see it from afar, they encompass it, and one of them says, A^aToriqo karaA A_in~aka laA turaY [or lano turaY (Meyd in explanation of the preceding prov.) i. e. Lower thine eyes, or be silent, karà: thou wilt not be seen: ] until he becomes within reach of it; when he throws a garment over it, and takes it. ('Eyn, TA.) And A^aToriqo karaA yuHolabo laka [ Lower thine eyes, or be silent, karà: milk shall be drawn for thee: ] is [a prov., mentioned by Meyd,] said to a stupid person whom one incites to hope for that which is vain, or false, and who believes [what is said to him]. (O.) ― -b5- One says also, ATrq A_ilaY All~ahowi (tropical:) He inclined to diversion, sport, or play. (IAar, K, TA.) ― -b6- ATrq All~ayolu Ealayohi :

6. -A2- ATrq AlS~ayoda He set a snare for the beasts, or birds, of the chase. (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, ATrq fulaAnN lifulaAnK (assumed tropical:) Such a one plotted against such a one by calumny, or slander, in order to throw him into destruction, or into that from which escape would be difficult. (TA.)
5 He found a way to such a thing: (MA:) or he sought to gain access to such a thing. (Er-Rághib, TA.)

6 signifies The coming consecutively, or being consecutive. (TA.) You say, tTArqt AlA_ibilu The camels came following one another, the head of each. [ except the first ] being at the tail of the next [ before it ], whether tied together in a file or not: (TA:) or went away, one after another; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ ; (O, K, TA;) in the S, incorrectly, ↓ ; (O, K, TA;) in mentioned in the K, in another part of the art., and there expl. as meaning the followed one another; but the verb in this sense is ↓ : (TA:) and, (O, K, TA,) as some say, (O, TA,) this last signifies they scattered, or dispersed, themselves upon the roads, and quitted the main beaten tracks: (O, K, TA:) As cited as an ex., (from Ru-beh, TA,) describing camels, (O,) $atiytaA ↓ meaning They came together, and went away in a st

3. Said of the wing of a bird, (S, TA,) Its feathers overlay one another: (TA:) or it was, or became, abundant and dense [ in its feathers ]. (S, TA.) And AT~rqt AlA^aroDu The earth became disposed in layers, one above another, being compacted by the rain. (TA.) And AT~rq AlHawoDu The watering-trough, or tank, had in it [ a deposit of ] compacted dung, or dung and mud or clay, that had fallen into it. (TA.) And AT~rq Ealayohi All~ayolu , as in the O and L; in the K, erroneously, ↓ ; The night came upon him portion upon portion. (TA.) See also 6, in three places.

10 He desired, or demanded, of him a stallion to cover his she-camels; (S, O, K;) like AstDrbhu . (TA.) ― -b2- And AstTrqhu He desired, or demanded, of him the practising of pessomancy ( AlD~aroba biAlHaSaY ), and the looking [or divining ] for him therein. (K, * TA.) ― -b3- And He desired, or demanded, of him the [ having, or taking, a ] road, or way, within some one of his boundaries. (TA.) ― -b4- mino gayori A^ano yasotaToriqa naSiyba AlA=xari , a phrase used by El-Kudooree, means Without his taking for himself the portion of the other as a road or way [or place of passage ]. (Mgh.) And AlAisotiToraAqu bayona AlS~ufuwfi , a phrase used by Khwáhar-Zádeh [commonly pronounced KháharZádeh], means The going [or the taking for oneself a way ] between the ranks [of the people engaged in prayer
15.] ― -b5- [ A@sotaToraqato in a verse cited in the K in art. dd is a mistake for AstTrft , with fA : see
10 in art. Trb .]

[originally an inf. n., and as such app. signifying An act of striking the lute &c.: and hence,] a species ( DarobN ) of the A^aSowaAt [meaning sounds, or airs, or tunes, ] of the lute: (TA:) or any Sawot [i. e. air, or tune ], (Lth, O, K, TA,) or any nagomap [i. e. melody ], (K, TA,) of the lute and the like, by itself: (Lth, O, K, TA:) you say, taDoribu h`*ihi AljaAriyapu ka*aA waka*aA TaroqFA [ This girl, or young woman, or female slave, plays such and such airs or tunes, or such and such melodies, of the lute or the like ]. (Lth, O, K. *) ― -b2- [

Hence, probably,] Einodahu TuruwqN mina AlkalaAmi , sing. TaroqN , a phrase mentioned by Kr; thought by ISd to mean He has [ various ] sorts, or species, of speech. (TA.) ― -b3- See also TaroqapN , in four places. -A2- Also (tropical:) A stallion [ camel ] covering: (O, K, TA:) pl. TuruwqN and Tur~aAqN : (TA:) an inf. n. used as a subst. [or an epithet]: (O, K, TA:) for *uw TaroqK . (TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) The sperma of the stallion [camel]: (S, K:) a man says to another, A^aEironiY Taroqa faHolika AlEaAma i. e. [ Lend thou to me ] the sperma, and the covering, (As, TA.) which latter is said to be the original meaning, (TA,) of thy stallion [ camel this year ]. (As, TA.) And it is said to be sometimes applied metaphorically to (assumed tropical:) The sperma of man: or in relat

Also, and ↓ , (tropical:) Water (S, O, K, TA) of the rain (S, O, TA) in which camels (S, O, K) and others [i. e. other beasts ] have staled, (S,) or waded and staled, (S, * O, K, TA,) and dunged: (S, O, TA:) or stagnant water in which beasts have waded and staled: (Mgh:) and ↓ [expressly stated to be muHar~akap ] signifies [the same, or] water that has collected, in which there has been a wading and staling, so that it has become turbid; (TA;) or places where water collects and stagnates (S, O, K, TA) in stony tracts of land; (TA;) and the pl. of this is A^aToraAqN . (TA.) -A4- TaroqN also signifies A [ snare, trap, gin, or net, such as is commonly called ] fax~ , (IAar, O, K,) or the like thereof; and so ↓ : (K: [by Golius and Freytag, this meaning has been assigned to TaroqapN ; and by F
: see TaroqapN . -A2- [Also a contraction of TuruqN , pl. of TariyqN , q. v.] -A3- And pl. of TiraAqN [q. v.]. (K.)

Fat, as a subst.: (S, O, K:) this is the primary signification. (S, O.) [See an ex. voce bin~N .] ― -b2- And Fatness. (AHn, K.) One says, h`*aA AlbaEiyru maA bih TiroqN i. e. This camel has not in him fatness, and fat. (AHn, TA.) It is said to be mostly used in negative phrases. (TA.) ― -b3- And Strength: (S, O, K:) because it mostly arises from fat. (S, O.) One says, maA bihi TiroqN , meaning There is not in him strength. (TA.) The pl. is A^aToraAqN . (TA.) -A2- See also TaroqN , last quarter.
: see TaroqN , third quarter. ― -b2- Also i. q. mu*al~alN [applied to a beast, app. to a camel,] meaning Rendered submissive, or tractable

senses.text: 1 , (K,) aor. , (TK,) inf. n. TalomN , (TA,) He made the cake of bread even, or equable. (K.)

2 , inf. n. taToliymN , He beat a cake of bread baked in hot ashes with his hand, (K, TA) in order that it might become cool. (TA.) Hence the saying of Hassán. taZal~u jiyaAdunaA mutamaT~iraAtK yuTal~imuhun~a biAlxumuri Aln~isaA='u (K, * TA:) or, as some relate it, yulaT~imuhun~a ; but this is weak, or repudiated: (K:) or this is the correct reading, and the more obviously appropriate in meaning, accord. to MF; and accord. to IAth, it is the reading commonly known, and the same as the former in meaning: (TA:) the meaning is, [ Our coursers passing the day running like the pouring of rain, ] the women wiping the sweat from them with the mufflers: (K, TA:) or, as some say, [ the women with the mufflers ] beating them with the hands in removing the dust that was upon them. (TA.)

TulamN . (L, TA.) It is said in a prov., A_in~a duwna AlT~alomapi xaroTa qataAdi huwobara (Meyd, TA) [i. e. Before the attainment of the cake of bread baked in hot ashes is the stripping of the leaves, by grasping each branch and drawing the hand down it, of the tragacanth of Howbar ]: the Tulomap is the cake of bread that is put in hot ashes; and Howbar is a place abounding with the tragacanth: the prov. is applied in relation to a thing that is unattainable. Zalilotu , (T, S, M, O, Msb, K,) [and accord. to SM Zalalotu also, for he says that] the verb is of the class of manaEa as well as of the class of taEiba , (TA,) and Zalotu , (T, S, * M, O, K,) likened to lasotu , (M, K, *) formed by rejecting the former l in Zalilotu , (T, O,) and Zilotu , which is [also] originally Zalilotu , (Sb, T, M, O, K,) formed by transferring to the Z the vowel of the rejected l , (Sb, T, M, O,) anomalously, (Sb, M,) the latter of the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz; (T;) aor. yaZal~u ; (S, * M, O, * Msb, K;) imperative AiZolalo and Zalo (T) [and it is implied in the M voce qar~a that one says also AiZolilo and Zilo , which indicates that the aor. is also yaZil~u , but this requires confirmation, which I have not anywher
; or he passed his day fasting ]: (Lth, T:) and Zal~a nahaArahu yafoEalu ka*aA [ He was in, or during, his day doing such a thing
; or he passed his day doing such a thing ]: (M, K:) and Zalilotu A^aEomalu ka*aA [ I was in the day or daytime, or I passed the day, doing such a thing

; or] I did such a thing in the day or daytime. (S, O, Msb. *) In the saying of 'Antarah, walaqado A^abiytu EalaY AlT~awaY waA^aZal~uhu Hat~aY A^anaAla bihi kariyma AlmaA^okali [app. meaning And verily I pass the night in hunger, and I pass the day in it, that I may attain thereby plentiful eating ], A^aZal~uhu is for A^aZal~u Ealayohi . (S, O.) And accord. to some, (TA,) Zal~a layolahu occurs in poetry; (M, K, TA;) so that one says, Zal~a layolahu yafoEalu ka*aA [ He was in, or during, his night, or he passed his night, doing such a thing ]: but it is said that in this case the verb has the meaning next following. (TA.) ― -b2- And it signifies also He, or it, became; syn. SaAra : (Er-Rághib, TA:) being in this sense likewise an incomplete [i. e. a non-attributive] verb, divested of that m

60 and xliii. 16], Zal~a wajohuhu musowad~FA [ His face becomes black ]: so says Ibn-Málik: (TA:) or this may mean his face continues all the day black: (Bd in xvi. 60:) and one says also, Zal~a yafoEalu ka*aA meaning He continued doing such a thing: this too is mentioned by Ibn-Málik, and is of the dial. of the people of Syria. (TA.) ― -b3- It is also a complete [i. e. an attributive] verb as meaning He, or it, continued; as is said in the Expos. of the “ Shifè, ” and by Ibn-Málik; and, as Ibn-Málik likewise says, it was, or became, long. (TA.)

(M.) ― -b2- [And Zll~`hu signifies He shaded him, or it. See an ex. in a verse of Jereer in art. rdf , conj.

3.] l`kino EalaY AlA^avalaAti laHomN laA yuZal~alu [ But at the tamarisk-trees is flesh that will not be shaded, or, accord. to the reading given by Meyd, biAlA^avalaAti ,] is a prov., said by Beyhes, in allusion to the flesh of his slain brothers, on the occasion of persons saying, Zal~iluwA laHoma jazuwrikumo [ Shade ye the flesh of your slaughtered camel ]. (S, O.) -A2- See also
4. -A3- One says also Zl~l biAls~awoTi , meaning He made a sign with the whip for the purpose of frightening. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.)

4 , said of a day, It was, (S, O,) or became, (M, K,) shady, or a day having shade: (S, M, O, K:) or it was a day having clouds, or other [ causes of shade ]: (T:) or it was continually shady; as also ↓ , aor. yaZil~u , inf. n. ZilaAlapN . (Msb.) ― -b2- And, said of a thing, [ It extended its shade

; or] its shade extended; as also ↓ . (Msb.) -A2- A^aZal~atoniY Al$~ajarapu [ The tree shaded me, or afforded me shade ]: and in like manner one says of other things than trees. (S, O.) A^aZal~aka said of a building, or of a mountain, or of a cloud, means It protected thee, and cast its shade upon thee. (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] AZl~hu (assumed tropical:) He took him into his shelter, or protection: (TA:) or he guarded, or protected, him, and placed him within the scope of his might, or power of resistance or defence. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b3- And A^aZal~aniY (assumed tropical:) It (a thing) covered me: (M, K:) or it approached me, or drew near to me, so as to cast its shade upon me: (K:) or it has both of these meanings: (M:) or A^aZal~aka means he, (T, S,) or it, (O,) approached thee, or drew

5 see the next paragraph. It is also pronounced taZal~aY : (IAar, T:) and signifies He kept to shady places, and to ease, or repose: (IAar, T and K in art. ZlY :) it is like taZan~ayotu from AlZ~an~u . (T in that art.)

10 , (T,) or AstZl~ biAliZ~il~i , (Msb, TA,) He (a man, T) sheltered, or protected, himself by means of the shade: (T, TA:) or the latter means he inclined to the shade and sat in it. (M, K.) And AstZl~ mina Al$~aYo'i and bihi means ↓ [i. e. he shaded himself ( tZl~l being quasi-pass. of Zal~alahu ) from the thing and by means of it ]. (M, K.) You say, AstZl~ bihi mina Al$~amosi [ He shaded himself with it, or by means of it, from the sun ]. (T.) And AstZl~ biAl$~ajarapi He shaded and sheltered himself by means of the tree. (Ibn-'Abbád, S, O.) ― -b2- AstZl~ Ald~amu The blood was in the jawof [or belly, or interior of the belly, or the chest ]. (T, O, K, TA. [In the CK, mn Aljawofi is put for fiY Aljawofi .]) ― -b3- AstZl~t AlEayonu , (T, Ibn-'Abbád, O,) or AlEuyuwnu , (K,) The eye, (T, Ibn

properly signifies Shade; i. e. the light of the sun without the rays: when there is no light, it is ZulomapN , not Zil~N : (S, O:) contr. of DiH~N : (M, K:) or i. q. faYo'N : (K:) so some say: (M:) or so the [common] people say: (IKt, Msb:) or the former is [ shade ] in the morning; and the latter is in the evening: (M, K:) or, accord. to IKt, the former is in the morning and in the evening; but the latter is only after the declining of the sun from the meridian: ISk says that the former is from the rising of the sun to its declining; and the latter, from the declining to the setting: Th says that the Zil~ of a tree &c. is in the morning; and the faYo' , in the evening: (Msb:) Ru-beh says, (M, Msb,) any place, (M,) or any thing, (Msb,) upon which the sun has been and which it has quitted

; or disapproved, as in waZil~K mino yaHomuwmK in the Kur [lvi. 42, meaning And shade of smoke, or black smoke ]. (TA.) And AlZ~ilaAlu means ZilaAlu Aljan~api [ The shades of Paradise ]: (Fr, T, O, K, TA:) in some copies of the K, waAlZ~ilaAlu Aljan~apu , which is a mistake: (TA:) [but this requires consideration; for] El-'Abbás Ibn- 'Abd-El-Muttalib says, mino qabolihaA Tibota fiY AlZ~ilaAli wafiY musotawodaEK Hayovu yuxoSafu Alwaraqu [ Before it thou wast good in, or in the shades of, Paradise, and in a depositary in the part where leaves are sewed together to conceal the pudenda ]; (T, O, TA;) i. e. before thy descent to the earth (to which the pronoun in qblhA relates), thou wast good in the loins of Adam when he was in Paradise. (TA.) Aljan~apu taHota ZilaAli Als~uyuwfi [ Paradise is
; or power of resistance or defence: (M, K, TA:) whence [as some say] its usage in the Kur xiii. 35, and the usage of [the pl.] ZilaAl in xxxvi.

56 and in lxxvii. 41: [but the primary signification is more appropriate in these instances:] and so in the saying, jaEalaniY fiY Zil~ihi [i. e. (assumed tropical:) He placed me within the scope of his might, or power of resistance or defence ]: so says Er-Rághib. (TA.) ― -b10- And (assumed tropical:) A state of life ample in its means or circumstances, unstraitened, or plentiful, and easy, pleasant, soft, or delicate. (TA.) ― -b11- Also (assumed tropical:) The beginning of winter. (T, O. [Accord. to the copies of the K, of youthfulness: but I think that Al$~abaAb in this instance, in the K, is evidently a mistranscription for Al$~itaA=' .]) And (assumed tropical:) The vehemence (T, O, K) of the heat (T, O) of summer. SiH~apN : thus accord. to the copies of the K; but this may be a mistranscription; for Az and others mention, among the significations of Zl~p , [in a copy of the T, written in this case, as in others, ↓ ,] that of SayoHapN [q. v.]. (TA.)

A thing that covers, or protects, [or shades, ] one, overhead: accord. to Lth, i. q. ↓ or miZal~apN meaning a thing that shades one from the sun: (T:) see an ex. voce miZal~apN : a covering: and i. q. buroTul~apN : (M, K:) this latter word correctly signifies a miZal~ap for the summer: (TA in art. brTl :) and a thing by which one is protected from the cold and the heat: (M:) anything that protects and shades one, as a building or a mountain or a cloud: (Mgh:) the first portion that shades (AZ, S, K) of a cloud (AZ, S) or of clouds; (K;) accord. to Er-Rághib, mostly said of that which is deemed unwholesome, and which is disliked; whence the use of the word in the Kur vii. 170: (TA:) and what shades one, of trees: (K:) or anything that forms a covering over one, (T, TA,) or shades one: (T:)
i. q. ZilaAlN ; (T, K, TA;) app. a pl. of ZaliylN , like as Til~apN is of TaliylN . (TA.)
Water that is beneath a tree, (O,) or beneath trees, (K,) upon which the sun does not come. (O, K.) [See also DalalN .]
, like saHaAbN , [so accord. to the K, but in my copies of the S, ↓ ,] A thing that shades one, (IAar, S, O, K, TA,) such as a cloud, (IAar, S, TA,) and the like. (IAar, TA.) [See also Zul~apN .]
pl. of Zil~N : (S, M, O, K:) ― -b2- and of Zul~apN . (M, K.) ― -b3- [
Also, app., pl. of ZaliylN : see Zil~apN . ― -b4- Freytag has app. understood it to be expl. in the K as syn. with maZal~apN ; though it certainly is not.] ― -b5- See also ZalaAlN .

A place having shade: (M, K:) or having constant shade. (T, S, M, O, K.) And hence Zil~N ZaliylN (M, K) Constant shade: (S:) or extensive shade: (O:) or in this case the latter word denotes intensiveness [meaning dense ]; (M, K, TA;) being like $aAEirN in the phrase $iEorN $aAEirN . (TA.) Zil~FA ZaliylFA in the Kur iv.

60 is said by Er-Rághib to be an allusion to ease and pleasantness of life. (TA.) One says also A^ayokapN ZaliylapN A collection of trees tangled, or luxuriant, or abundant and dense. (TA.) In the saying of Uheyhah Ibn-El-Juláh, describing palm-trees, hiYa AlZ~il~u fiY AlHar~i Haq~a AlZ~ali li waAlmanoZaru AlA^aHosanu AlA^ajomalu The final character of line one and the initial character of line two are unclear. [ISd says] in my opinion, he means Al$~aYo'u AlZ~aliylu Haq~a AlZ~aliyli ; [so that the verse should be rendered They are the shade in the heat, the shady thing, the extremely shady, and the most goodly, the most beautiful, thing at which one looks; (see the phrase h`*aA AlEaAlimu Haq~a AlEaAlimi , voce Haq~N ;)] the inf. n. being put in the place of the subst. , (M, TA,) with fet-h, (TA,) the subst. from the verb in the phrase Zal~alonaA Ealayohimu AlgamaAma [expl. above, see 2; as such app. meaning either The making to give shade, like the inf. n. taZoliylN , or a thing that gives shade, like ZilaAlapN ]. : see Zul~apN . ― -b2- Also A cloud that one sees by itself, and of which one sees the shadow upon the earth. (K.) ― -b3- And one says, raA^ayotu ZilaAlapF mina AlT~ayori i. e. gayaAbapF [app. meaning I saw a covert, or place of concealment, of birds ]. (TA.)

A place in which a little water collects and stagnates in a water-course and the like: (Lth, T:) or a place in which water collects and stagnates in the lower part of the torrent of a valley: (M, K:) or the like of an excavated hollow in the interior of a water-course, such that the water stops, and remains therein: (AA, O:) pl. ZalaAy^ilu . (Lth, AA, T, O.) And A meadow ( rawoDap ) abounding with collections of trees, or of dense and tangled trees: (AA, T, O, K:) pl. as above. (K.)

i. q. suEonN , i. e. A ↓ [q. v.

; or as expl. in the L, in art. sEn , a Zul~ap (q. v.), or a thing like the Zul~ap , which is made upon the flat house-tops, for the purpose of guarding against the dew that comes from the direction of the sea in the time of the greatest heat ]; on the authority of IAar. [ More, and most, dense in shade ]. The Arabs say, layosa $aYo'N A^aZal~a mino HajarK [ There is not anything more dense in shade than a stone ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And A^aZal~ , [as a subst., i. e. A^aZal~N accord. to a general rule, or, if regarded as originally an epithet, it may be A^aZal~u ,] by poetic license A^aZolal , (S, M, O, K,) signifies The under part, (S, O,) or the concealed part, (M, AHei, K,) of the manosim , (S, M, O, K,) or of the xuf~ , (AHei, TA,) [the former app. here used, as it is said be in other cases, in the same sense as the latter, meaning the foot, ] of the camel; (S, M, O, AHei, K;) so called because of its being concealed: (AHei, TA:) and, (M, K,) in a human being, (M,) AlA^aZal~u signifies baTonu AlA_iSobaEi ; (M, K;) and [ISd says] this is in my opinion the righ

A thing having shade; by means of which one shades himself; as also ↓ . (Msb.) And [A cloudy day;] a day having clouds: or having continual shade. (TA.)

(T, S, M, Msb, K) and maZal~apN , (T, M, Msb, K,) the former with kesr to the m as an instrumental noun, (Msb,) [and the latter with fet-h as a noun of place,] A large tent of [ goats' ] hair; (S, O, Msb;) more ample than the xibaA=' ; so says El-Fárábee: (Msb:) one of the kinds of tents of the Arabs of the desert, the largest of the tents of [ goats' ] hair; next after which is the wasuwT ; and then, the xibaA=' , which is the smallest of the tents of [goats'] hair; so says AZ: but Aboo-Málik says that the mZl~p and the xbA=' are small and large: IAar says that the xayomap is of poles roofed with [the panic grass called] vamaAm , and is not of cloths; but the mZl~p is of cloths: (T:) or it is of the tents called A^axobiyap ; (M;) such as is large, of the A^axobiyap ; (K;) and it is said t

Hence, as being likened thereto, (assumed tropical:) A booth, or shed, made of palm-sticks, and covered with [ the panic grass called ] vumaAm . (Msb.) ― -b3- And The thing [i. e. umbrella ] by means of which kings are shaded on the occasion of their riding; called in Pers. Jator . (TA.)
[ A booth, or shed, shaded over ] is from AlZ~il~u . (S.)
: see muZil~N .

Blood that is in the jawof [or belly, or interior of the belly, or the chest ]. (T, O.) ― -b2- And [Az says,] I heard a man of the tribe of Teiyi apply the term AlmusotaZil~aAtu [so accord. to a copy of the T, but in the TA AlmusotaZil~u ,] to Certain thin flesh, adhering to the interior of the two fetlock-joints of the camel, than which there is in the flesh of the camel none thinner, nor any softer, but there is in it no grease. senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. ZaloEN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) said of a camel, (S, O, Msb, K,) and of a man also, (Msb, TA,) and, by Aboo-Dhu-eyb, of a horse, (S, TA,) [and likewise said of a dog, (see ZaAliEN ,)] He limped, or halted, syn. gamaza fiY ma$oyihi , (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) and Earija ; (TA;) or was slightly lame: (Mgh:) what it signifies resembles EarajN [or natural lameness], and therefore it is said to be a slight Earaj . (Msb.) One says, Airoqa EalaY ZaloEika , (S, O, L, K,) a prov., (O, L,) meaning Ascend thou the mountain with knowledge [or because ] of thy limping, or slight lameness, not jading thyself: (L:) or deal gently with thyself, and burden not thyself with more than thou art able to do: (S:) or impose upon thyself, of what is difficult, [ only ] what thou art able to do; for he

Also, said of a man, (tropical:) He stopped short, and lagged behind. (TA.) ― -b3- ZalaEati AlA^aroDu biA^aholihaA (tropical:) The land became straitened with its inhabitants, by reason of their multitude; (A 'Obeyd, S, O, K;) it would not bear them, by reason of their multitude, like the beast that limps with its load because of its heaviness. (Z, TA.) ― -b4- ZalaEat said of a bitch, (tropical:) She desired copulation. (As, O, K, TA.) And ZalaEa said of a dog, (assumed tropical:) He desired to copulate. (TA.) -A2- ZalaEato EayonahaA She (a woman) contracted and inclined her eye. (TA.)
4 He made his camel, or beast, that he rode, to limp, or become lame. (A, TA.)

5 In the following saying of a poet, wamaA *aAka mino juromK A^atayotuhumu bihi walaA HasadK min~iY lahumo yataZal~aEu ISd thinks the meaning to be, [ And that was not a crime, or an offence, that I committed against them, nor envy on my part ] arising in their minds, and occurring hastily to their understandings. (TA.)
, thus with fet-h to the l , A declining from the truth, or from that which is right; and a sin, crime, fault, or misdeed. (TA.)
A disease in the legs of a beast, not from journeying nor from fatigue, (Lth, K, TA, [in the O inadvertently written DulaAE ,]) in consequence of which it limps. (Lth, TA.)

Limping, or halting; [or slightly lame; ] applied to a camel, and a horse, [&c.,] (S,) [i. e.,] to a beast, (TA,) to the male and the female alike, (Lth, O, K, TA,) to the former as a part. n., and to the latter as a possessive noun, (TA,) like gaAmizN ; (Lth, O, TA;) or the fem. of ZaAliEN is ZaAliEapN , (S, O, K, TA,) but one does not say gaAmizapN : (O, TA:) [pl. Zul~aEN .] One says, laA A^anaAmu Hat~aY yanaAma ZaAliEu AlkilaAbi [ I will not sleep until the limping dog sleeps ]; (O, K;) a prov., (O,) meaning, until the dogs become still; (O, K;) because the ZAlE , of dogs, waits until there remains none other, and then copulates, and sleeps: (As, O, K:) ― -b2- or the ZAlE is the dog that is lusting for the female; for such does not sleep; and the saying is applied to him who is mindful
, applied to a load, i. q. muDoliEN [i. e. Heavily burdening, or overburdening, &c.
